ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution}: It can be known from the graph that when $-2<x<-1$, $y_1>y_2$. Therefore, when $x$ takes values in the range $(-2,-1)$, $y_1>y_2$ holds. Hence, the answer is $x\in\boxed{(-2,-1)}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the left half-plane of the figure, one branch of the hyperbola $y_2=\frac{k}{x}\,(x<0)$ is drawn, and the line $y_1=x+m$ with positive slope intersects it at two points D and C; it can be seen from the figure that between D and C, the line is above the hyperbola. The problem has already given the coordinates of point C as $(-1,2)$.

Reasoning: Since C$(-1,2)$ lies on the line $y_1=x+m$, we get $2=-1+m$, so $m=3$; since C$(-1,2)$ lies on the hyperbola $y_2=\frac{k}{x}$, we get $2=\frac{k}{-1}$, so $k=-2$. Thus the intersection points of the two graphs satisfy
$ x+3=\frac{-2}{x}$, that is, $x^2+3x+2=0$, solving gives $x=-2$ and $x=-1$. Combining with the graph, $y_1>y_2$ corresponds to the interval where the line is above the hyperbola, that is, the open interval between the abscissas of the two intersection points, so $x\in(-2,-1)$.
